[[Category:Asset]]
'''Properties''' are positive [[asset]]s owned by a [[legal entity]].<ref>{{#cite:Q3952}}</ref>

== Classification ==

A property can be:

* '''material''' or '''immaterial''': e.g, a house v. copyright over a book ([[intellectual property]]);
* '''exclusive''', '''shared''', or '''public''': owned by one [[legal entity]], jointly owned by multiple legal entities, or owned by a [[government]];
* '''mobile''' or '''immobile'''¹: e.g, a mobile phone v. an acre of farm land;
* '''disposable''' or '''non-disposable''': a bicycle you own v. a debt someone owes to you³;

<blockquote>
1:
{| class="wikitable"
|-
! Proper terminology in [[jurisdiction]]
! Mobile property
! Immobile property
|-
| France

|-

2: Somewhat counterintuitively, '''personal property''' is also used to designate mobile properties owned by organisations.

3: Debt owed by other legal entities are considered part of property. However, this property is completely '''non-disposable''' until the debt is recovered.
</blockquote>

<blockquote>
In some [[jurisdiction]]s, animals, or even human beings can be considered property of someone. In other jurisdictions, such as France, this is never the case.<ref>{{#cite:Q3952}}</ref>
</blockquote>

== Ownership ==

To be considered the '''legal owner''' of a property, one must have acquired it lawfully.

=== Rights of owner ===

When one owns a property, one can, unless a law forbids it:

* Use it;
* Move it;
* Transform it;
* Rent it;
* Use it as [[collateral]] to obtain a bank loan;
* Dispose of it (sell, convert, destroy, etc.).

==== In case of death ====

In many jurisdictions, a person continues to exercise the '''right of disposal''' on their property after death.

Therefore, a person is free to establish a '''[[will]]'''.

When no will is established, their properties are often divided between their relatives, especially their life partner and children, according to proportions established by law.

<ref>{{#cite:Q3952}}</ref>
